topIssues.body:
See design-doc: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/blob/main/protocol/deprecate-reqresp-sync.md

This aims to fix sync problems seen with the old req-resp protocol based syncing.

The related op-node CLI flags need deprecation, and sync behavior needs to change as described in the design-doc.
The CLI sync-flag should be a no-op. 

An explicit `--skip-initial-l1-sync` should be introduced for users who aim to verify the chain starting after an initial EL sync.

topIssues.title: op-node: sequencer LightCL performs needless engine reset on every restart (may rewind EL heads)
topIssues.author: opsuperchain
topIssues.body:
## Summary

An op-node configured as a "sequencer LightCL" — i.e. with both `--sequencer.enabled` and `--l2.follow.source` — runs `TryInitialResetEngineForSequencer` → `FindL2Heads` → `forceReset` on every process restart. The guard intended to make this a one-shot is based on in-process memory state that is always zero at fresh process start, so it never trips on restart. The reset re-walks the L2 chain against the current L1 view on every boot.

In the happy case this is wasteful. Under a stale/slow/reorged L1 RPC at restart, `FindL2Heads` can return heads earlier than what the EL already has correctly persisted, and `forceReset` will drive the EL backwards — a needless walkback. A LightCL should not need to walk back on a simple restart.

This is based on code review; I haven't reproduced a specific walkback incident from the restart path described.

## Code path

**Config gating** — [`op-node/service.go:372`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/op-node/service.go#L372):

```go
NeedInitialResetEngine: ctx.Bool(flags.SequencerEnabledFlag.Name) && l2FollowSourceEndpoint != "",
```

**Entry** — [`op-node/rollup/driver/sync_deriver.go:238-244`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/op-node/rollup/driver/sync_deriver.go#L238-L244):

```go
if s.SyncCfg.FollowSourceEnabled() {
    if s.SyncCfg.NeedInitialResetEngine {
        // May need a single reset to trigger sequencer block building
        s.Engine.TryInitialResetEngineForSequencer(s.Ctx)
    }
    return
}
```

**Insufficient guard** — [`op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go:1147-1163`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go#L1147-L1163):

```go
func (e *EngineController) TryInitialResetEngineForSequencer(ctx context.Context) {
    e.mu.Lock()
    defer e.mu.Unlock()
    if e.unsafeHead != (eth.L2BlockRef{}) {
        return
    }
    // ... FindL2Heads + forceReset
}
```

`EngineController` is process-scoped — `e.unsafeHead` is zero at process start regardless of datadir/EL state. The guard is effective within a single process after the first call, but does not prevent the reset from re-running across restarts.

## Impact

- **Always on restart**: unnecessary FCU round-trip and L1-canonicality walk of the L2 chain.
- **Under L1 RPC flakiness or partial L1 view at restart**: `FindL2Heads` can return heads earlier than the EL's persisted unsafe head, and `forceReset` will send a `ForkchoiceUpdated` telling the EL to rewind blocks that were validly derived and persisted.

## Fix directions (not prescriptive)

- Check the EL for an existing unsafe head before the guard, so the guard reflects persisted state rather than in-memory state.
- Persistent "initialized" marker in the datadir, consulted before running the reset.
- Gate the reset on "EL reports genesis as latest" so it only runs on truly fresh state.

## Not affected

Pure LightCL followers (follow-source without `--sequencer.enabled`) do not hit this path — `NeedInitialResetEngine` is false for them.

topIssues.title: Flaky: TestRelayWithInvalidMessagesSteady fails on transient EL dial timeout
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** This issue was filed by Claude (AI assistant) based on CircleCI flake data and failure artifacts.

## Test

- **Name:** `TestRelayWithInvalidMessagesSteady`
- **Package:** `github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/loadtest`
- **Test file:** `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/loadtest/invalid_msg_test.go`
- **Assertion site:** `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/loadtest/schedule.go:273`

## Recent flakes (CircleCI Insights)

| Pipeline | Job | Workflow date |
|----------|-----|---------------|
| [123327](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/123327/workflows/c6e21643-0e34-4615-ae7c-fc05f7ee0ea9/jobs/4891215) | `memory-all-kona-op-reth` | 2026-04-23 |
| [123217](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/123217) | `memory-all-opn-op-reth` | 2026-04-22 |
| [123082](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/123082) | `memory-all-kona-op-reth` | 2026-04-21 |

## Failure

```
assertions.go:387:
    Error Trace: op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/loadtest/schedule.go:273
    Error:       Received unexpected error:
                 dial tcp 127.0.0.1:45777: i/o timeout
--- FAIL: TestRelayWithInvalidMessagesSteady (181.92s)
```

Port `45777` is a proxy in front of `l2B`'s `op-reth` EL.

## Likely root cause

`Steady.Run` in `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/loadtest/schedule.go:251-296` spawns a polling goroutine that calls `s.el.InfoByLabel(t.Ctx(), eth.Unsafe)` every `blockTime` to sample gas usage for AIMD backpressure. On any non-context error it does `t.Require().NoError(err)` (line 273), which fails the whole test.

`TestRelayWithInvalidMessagesSteady` simultaneously spams 1,000 invalid executing messages per block time at the same `l2B` EL via the same proxy. Under that load, a transient `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:45777: i/o timeout` (e.g. TCP accept backlog saturation on the proxy) can occur. The check `errors.Is(err, t.Ctx().Err())` on line 270 only catches context cancellation, not transient network errors while the test is still running.

## Why flaky (not consistent)

The dial timeout is load/timing dependent. The poll fires roughly once per 2s, and the proxy/EL only saturates intermittently enough for a dial to time out. Every other goroutine in this test treats EL errors as non-fatal — only this Steady poll treats them as fatal.

## Proposed fix

Make the Steady polling goroutine resilient to transient EL errors. Its purpose is to sample gas usage for backpressure, not to assert EL liveness. Log a warning, skip the adjustment, continue polling — matching the tolerance pattern in `schedule.go:325-333` and `invalid_msg_test.go:77`.

topIssues.title: interop: follow-up items from strong-consistency review
topIssues.author: karlfloersch
topIssues.body:
## Context

Follow-up items from Adrian's review of #19505 (interop: add strong consistency guarantees). These are the items that require more than a trivial fix.

## Items

### 1. Tests should pass a no-op `l1Checker` instead of nil check
[Review comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19505#discussion_r2937364078)

`l1Checker` is only ever nil in tests. Tests should pass a no-op l1Checker and the `if i.l1Checker != nil` guard in `observeRound` should be removed — not having an l1Checker in production would be a significant issue.

### 2. `Decision` enum WAL serialization resilience
[Review comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19505#discussion_r2937399214)

`Decision` is serialized to JSON as a bare integer via `iota`. If the enum order is ever changed or a new variant inserted, any pending WAL entry written by a previous binary would be silently misinterpreted on restart. Consider assigning explicit numeric values or using string-based serialization (`MarshalJSON`/`UnmarshalJSON` returning `"advance"`, `"invalidate"`, etc.).

### 3. Idempotent replay should compare deserialized structs, not raw bytes
[Review comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19505#discussion_r2937399277)

The idempotent replay check in `VerifiedDB.Commit()` uses `bytes.Equal` on JSON-serialized `VerifiedResult`. Go's `encoding/json` does not guarantee byte-stable output across Go versions. If a node crashes after `Commit()` succeeds but before `ClearPendingTransition()`, and restarts on a newer Go version, the re-serialized value could differ, turning an idempotent replay into a hard `ErrAlreadyCommitted` failure. Compare the deserialized structs instead.

### 4. Add rewind replay test after partial failure
[Review comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19505#discussion_r2937413264)

`TestPendingTransition_RecoverRewindPreservedOnFailure` verifies the WAL is preserved when rewind fails, but doesn't test the second attempt — the actual replay. Add a test that: (1) fails chain B on first attempt, (2) fixes chain B, (3) replays via `progressAndRecord`, (4) verifies both chains end up correct and the WAL is cleared.

### 5. Integration tests should exercise `progressAndRecord` directly
[Review comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19505#discussion_r2937429822)

The compat shims used by `TestInterop_FullCycle` and most `TestProgressInterop*` tests bypass the WAL entirely. The core correctness property (WAL write → apply → clear) is not exercised. Two suggestions:
- Add an integration test using `progressAndRecord` directly for multiple advance cycles
- Add an end-to-end test for L1-inconsistency → rewind through `progressAndRecord`

### 6. Pass `frontierView` through call chain instead of storing as struct field
[Review comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19505#discussion_r2937449091)

Non-blocking nit: `frontierView` is only non-nil during `verify()` but as a struct field it looks like persistent state. Passing it through the call chain would make the lifetime explicit in the type signatures. Requires updating `verifyFn`/`cycleVerifyFn` function types and ~10-12 test stubs.

### 7. Narrow `ChainContainer` interface so reorg-triggering operations are only accessible to interop
[Review comments](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19505#discussion_r2937526917) / [also](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19505#discussion_r2937529321)

The TODO about removing the footgun (reorg-triggering operations exposed on ChainContainer) appears four times across `chain_container.go` and `invalidation.go`. This tracking issue captures that follow-up: move reorg-triggering operations behind a smaller interop-owned interface so that `RewindEngine` and `InvalidateBlock` are only callable from interop transition application.

### 8. Remove legacy DenyRecord backward compatibility after devnet reset
[Review comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19505#discussion_r2937413341)

Once the internal devnet is reset, remove the legacy `decodeDenyRecords` backward-compatibility path (concatenated 32-byte hashes). Knowing that all `DenyRecord` instances have a `DecisionTimestamp` would simplify reasoning about the code.

## Related PR
- #19505

## Summary
- bump the Rust OP stack to `revm 38`
- update related `alloy-evm`, `alloy-op-evm`, `op-revm`, `revm-inspectors`, and reth dependencies
- adapt `alloy-op-evm`, kona precompiles, and op-reth integration points to the new APIs

## Validation
- `cargo check -p alloy-op-evm -p reth-optimism-payload-builder -p reth-optimism-node -p kona-client`

## Follow-ups / caveats
- `alloy-op-evm` still derefs to `op_revm::OpContext<DB>` while the wrapper transaction type is `OpTx`, so the `ContextTr::Tx` mismatch is still present and not resolved in this branch
- the FPVM precompile provider currently hardcodes a `0` reservoir when invoking precompiles; this branch compiles, but reservoir-aware gas accounting likely still needs a follow-up review under the revm 38 / EIP-8037 model
